about.title: Galt Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Slip and fall accidents in Galt happen in places most people visit without a second thought — grocery aisles off A Street, apartment walkways near Twin Cities Road, parking lots along SR-99, or retail entrances on C Street. What starts as a wet floor, broken step, or poor lighting can end in a serious injury and a confusing claims process. California law requires showing the property owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and failed to address it. That means evidence matters — photos of the condition, witness names, and store surveillance footage that many businesses only keep for a short time before it's erased. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we connect injured Galt residents with an independent attorney who can evaluate the property, the timeline, and what proof exists. The consultation costs nothing, and there's no fee unless the attorney recovers compensation on your behalf.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Property Fixes the Problem

items.title: Notice Has to Be Proven
items.desc: California requires showing the owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney can dig into maintenance logs, prior complaints, and inspection records to establish that notice.

items.title: Surveillance Footage Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Galt businesses overwrite security video within days or weeks. Getting a preservation request out quickly can be the difference between having proof and having nothing.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: Even if you're partly blamed for not seeing a hazard, California's pure comparative fault rule still allows recovery for the percentage that wasn't your fault.

items.question: I fell at a store near SR-99 in Galt — what should I do first?
items.answer: Report the fall to store management and ask that an incident report be created, then photograph the hazard, your injuries, and the surrounding area before anything changes. Get the names of any witnesses if possible. Reach out promptly so an attorney can send a written request to preserve any surveillance video before it's deleted.

items.question: How long do I have to file a premises liability claim in California?
items.answer: Generally you have two years from the date of the fall, though claims against a public entity (like a city-owned building) often carry a much shorter deadline, sometimes just six months. Missing these windows can end a claim before it starts, so it's worth getting a free evaluation early.

items.question: Can I still recover money if I was partly distracted when I fell?
items.answer: Possibly, yes. California follows pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation can be reduced by your share of responsibility but isn't automatically wiped out. An independent attorney can help assess how fault might be divided in your specific situation.
